title: Mechanisms, choices and the experience of play
unit: One reviewed answer document to one open question

questions.Themes: Why themes feel strong or weak

topics.label: Internal balance & list choice
topics.definition: Model or theme variety, mandatory picks, redundant alternatives, missing options and the gap between a faction's best build and its wider roster.
topics.include: Explicit choice constraints, auto-includes, outdated or missing profiles, narrow competitive builds and praised roster breadth.
topics.exclude: Model availability mentioned only as a general reason for a theme rating belongs to theme-value. A strong profile alone belongs to balance.

topics.label: Theme benefits & restrictions
topics.definition: The exchange between recruitment restrictions, theme bonuses, synergies and the underlying model pool.
topics.include: Reasons a theme rewards, limits, duplicates or fails to support its permitted models; strong and weak themes both count.
topics.exclude: A faction-level complaint without reference to theme construction. A theme name alone qualifies only when its power or utility is explicitly assessed.

topics.label: Matchups, immunities & counters
topics.definition: Opposing toolkits, narrow counters, blanket immunities and the ability to answer an opponent's core plan.
topics.include: Specific favourable or difficult matchups, missing counter-tools, Soulless, anti-camouflage, fear resistance, binary effects and list-pair dependence.
topics.exclude: Generic dissatisfaction without an opponent, counter or immunity. Describing a weak faction alone belongs to balance.

topics.label: Interaction, control & negative play
topics.definition: Ability to act, fight, target, move or contest the opponent’s plan, plus explicit negative-play-experience complaints.
topics.include: Explicit NPE or non-interaction, prison references, restrictive control, inaccessible targets, gotchas and effects described as bypassing counterplay.
topics.exclude: An unfavourable matchup alone. Shooting or high damage alone belongs to damage.

topics.label: Activations, passes & model count
topics.definition: How action supply, waiting, extra activations, summoning and the number of models shape timing advantage.
topics.include: Outwaiting, pass tokens, activation stealing, low-count vulnerability and numerical swarms.
topics.exclude: Mobility without an action-economy explanation. Ki supply alone belongs to ki.

topics.label: Power & points efficiency
topics.definition: Direct judgements of faction, model or theme power and comparative value for Rice.
topics.include: Over- or underpowered profiles, external faction gaps, undercosting, overcosting and explicit overall balance assessments.
topics.exclude: Ordinary description of a faction's strengths and weaknesses without a power/value judgement. No strength is inferred from silence.

topics.label: Damage, shooting & early swings
topics.definition: Lethality, ranged pressure, alpha strikes and the consequences of early damage.
topics.include: Ranged threats, size-related shooting damage, early removal, attack output and weak hitting power.
topics.exclude: A model's name alone, even if it is a well-known shooter. Defensive characteristics belong to resilience.

topics.label: Armour, wounds & staying power
topics.definition: Ability to survive damage, hold a position and recover from attrition.
topics.include: Armour, wounds, regeneration, recursion, Durable or Last Stand, fragile profiles and overwhelming durability.
topics.exclude: Mental or state immunity discussed purely as a counter belongs to matchups. Slow movement alone belongs to mobility.

topics.label: Movement & positioning
topics.definition: Speed, placement, engagement choice, positioning demands and spatial reach.
topics.include: Outmanoeuvring, slow factions, charge dependence, terrain control, line of sight and catching or escaping opposing models.
topics.exclude: Waiting for a later activation without a spatial component. Scoring constraints alone belong to scenario.

topics.label: Ki supply & resource engines
topics.definition: Ki generation, transfer, shortage and the synergies or support chains they enable.
topics.include: Free Ki, summoning fuel, focus/transfer bottlenecks, Ki-starved themes and recurring resource provision.
topics.exclude: A Ki stat mentioned only for fear resistance or an opposed test, without a supply/use constraint.

topics.label: Dice control & reliability
topics.definition: Rerolls, Preordain, critical effects, automatic versus opposed resolution and the impact of failed rolls.
topics.include: Predictability, dice substitution, unmitigated variance, reroll access and explicit critical-attack comments.
topics.exclude: The number of dice used solely as a comparison of raw profile value. That belongs to balance.

topics.label: Scoring & game timing
topics.definition: Scenario access, scoring effects, objectives, game duration and the timing of useful bonuses.
topics.include: Free scenario actions, scoring cards, VIM, zone-holding, portal timing, late bonuses and games ending before completion.
topics.exclude: A late activation without reference to scenario or the timing of the game. A named event card alone is insufficient.

topics.label: Releases, errata & playtesting
topics.definition: Change over time: power creep, release pace, balance updates, playtesting and support for older models.
topics.include: Positive and negative errata accounts, perceived overcorrection, missing future support, frequent releases and testing concerns.
topics.exclude: A currently weak model without a development or support claim.

topics.label: Rules access & complexity
topics.definition: Finding, understanding and applying rules and interactions.
topics.include: Scattered documents, card bloat, unintuitive wording, loopholes and exploit complaints.
topics.exclude: A well-understood mechanic described as too strong; that is coded by its mechanism.

topics.label: Faction identity & model appeal
topics.definition: The connection between faction character, aesthetic or thematic appeal and what is rewarding to field.
topics.include: Faction identity diluted by common models, lore/model appeal, desired play style and lost thematic options.
topics.exclude: Every statement that a game is enjoyable. Ronin access without an identity claim belongs to ronin.

topics.label: Ronin access & shared staples
topics.definition: The place of cross-faction models and cards within faction rosters.
topics.include: Ronin recruitment, Hozumi enabling Ronin, shared staple cards, desired access and concerns about homogenisation.
topics.exclude: Assumed Ronin status of an otherwise unexplained named model.

topics.label: Learning, workload & retention
topics.definition: Practice, execution difficulty, new-player experience, keeping up with releases and continued participation.
topics.include: Learning curves, low error tolerance, discouragement, local play availability and reduced interest or play.
topics.exclude: A bare refusal to rate unfamiliar factions; this is recorded as an experience limit rather than a thematic finding.

methods: Every document was read in full and assigned individually against this codebook. Assignments are many-to-many; repeated wording within one answer counts once per topic.
Counts refer to answer documents. One submission can contribute an answer to each of three questions. Public texts have independent document IDs and no linked player profile.
Question counts use their own written-answer denominator. The prompts ask about problems, strong/weak themes and faction matchups; this shapes what people discuss.
Brief answers and statements declining assessment remain visible with a separate disposition. All reviewed documents remain in the counting denominator.
Explicitly positive overall assessments are tagged separately. Mentions of a mechanic can describe a strength, a problem or a trade-off; read the linked wording for the position taken.
This first pass was prepared by Codex with AI assistance, using the reviewed public corpus. One coding pass was completed; independent second-coder agreement has not been assessed.

Editorial interpretations and proposed follow-ups are authored separately from the counts. Rebuilding validates source hashes and recalculates membership, question counts and overlaps. New or changed answers enter the review queue.
Results describe these written accounts. The analysis uses no player-profile joins, significance tests or inferred faction win rates.
